headline.caveat: Contract dollars undisclosed. Samsung supplies HBM to NVIDIA as the third vendor — a smaller allocation than SK Hynix/Micron after repeated HBM3E qualification delays; HBM4 qualification restored it to the Rubin-generation supply pool.

realized_to_date.caveat: Deliveries ongoing (HBM3E in China-bound and select SKUs earlier; HBM4 ramping 2026); customer-level figures undisclosed.

nature_md: Multi-year HBM supply from Samsung to NVIDIA — historically the lagging qualifier (HBM3E passed NVIDIA qualification late after yield/thermal issues), with HBM4 bringing Samsung back into the allocation mix for the Rubin generation alongside its 1c-DRAM ramp. Volumes and pricing undisclosed; industry-wide HBM is sold out through 2026 and Samsung + SK Hynix are separately parties to OpenAI's Stargate memory LOI (up to 900K DRAM wafers/mo by 2029). Samsung's NVIDIA relationship spans HBM supply, foundry competition (vs TSMC), and its own Anthropic-round investment — multi-directional exposure.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: NVIDIA books HBM purchases in COGS on delivery; second/third-source allocation is a deliberate de-risking strategy against SK Hynix concentration, worth paying qualification overhead for.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Samsung's memory division books revenue on delivery under LTAs; regaining NVIDIA HBM4 qualification was the swing factor in its 2026 memory-margin recovery. Customer-level disclosure is nil.

sources.notes: Samsung HBM4 qualification/allocation reporting; single-outlet Korean supply-chain sourcing — treat allocation details as medium-low confidence.
